title: Concurrent-region transparent failover controller (stream-aware traffic choreography)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our hosted API edge must support active-active multi-region operation for low-latency inference while preserving session and streaming continuity. Current failover strategies either (a) force-orphan long-poll/stream sessions when a region is shifted, or (b) add significant coordination latency for every request. Both outcomes violate SLOs for streaming customers and increase token-cost due to replays.

Goals:
- Provide transparent, low-latency active-active failover for both short RPCs and long-lived streaming sessions.
- Maintain SLOs: p95 tail latency <= 250ms for non-streaming gen, p99 <= 650ms; stream-success-rate >= 99.5% (sessions not aborted by failover).
- Ensure graceful degradation: predictable load-shedding and circuit-breaker behaviour under overload that minimizes user-visible errors for high-priority workloads.
- Operational runbook and observability hooks (dashboards, alerts) to validate and react to incidents.

Design overview: "Concurrent-region Transparent Failover Controller" (CTFC)
- Session affinity model: lightweight session-token bearing region preferences but with heartbeats recorded in a thin "session-index" (eventual consistency) replicated to a read-optimized store across regions. The index is not authoritative for live routing but used for fastest best-effort placement.
- Dual-path handshake (Graceful Stream Drain Handshake - GSDH): when shifting traffic away from a region, CTFC initiates a short-lived TCP/stream handoff where the source region sends final KV-cache diff and tail-token checkpoint to the destination; consumer SDKs support resumable streams via an idempotent resume token.
- Fast fallback: if GSDH cannot complete within 3s, requests fall back to a stateless compatible model variant (quantized/non-KV) for degraded latency but preserved availability.
- Circuit breakers: region-level breakers with multivariate triggers: CPU util > 85% for 30s, token-gen p99 latency > 1.5x baseline, or error-rate > 3% for 60s. Breakers transition regions through states: CLOSED -> SOFT-TRIP (rate-limit low-priority routes) -> HARD-TRIP (exclude from new session placement) -> RECOVERING (canary traffic).
- Load-shedding priority tiers: 
  * Tier 0 (critical): low-latency interactive chat; never shed unless HARD-TRIP and all regions exhausted.
  * Tier 1 (important): short generation requests, high SLA customers; shed progressively during SOFT-TRIP by 20% buckets.
  * Tier 2 (best-effort): embeddings, long-batch reranks; shed first.
- Traffic choreography & percentage rollout: use dynamic weighted routing with fast adjustments (1s step) during incidents. Canary plan uses 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% ramp across recovering region when transitioning back to CLOSED.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Key metrics to emit: active_streams_per_region, session_resume_success, session_abort_rate, kv_sync_latency, region_cpu, region_mem, model_token_throughput, per_model_p50/p95/p99_latency, failover_handshake_success_rate.
- Alerts: session_abort_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m or session_resume_success < 98% -> P0.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype GSDH in staging (2 weeks): lightweight resume token and checkpoint snapshotting for a single model (tuned to decoder-only family).
2) Add session-index replication and best-effort routing logic (3 weeks): ensure reads are low-latency and eventual-consistency safe.
3) Circuit-breaker engine with policy DSL and integration into routing plane (3 weeks).
4) Canary & rollouts, load-shedding policy enforcement, and SDK resume token support (2 weeks).
5) Runbook, dashboards, and chaos test-suite (simulated region failover, high CPU/latency spikes) (2 weeks).

Runbook highlights:
- Immediate triage steps: identify region breaker state, trigger streaming drain or start stateless fallback.
- Manual interventions: force-exclude region, escalate to infra for capacity scale-up.
- Recovery: verify session_resume_success and kv_sync_latency before re-weighting region >5%.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for resume token semantics and idempotent replay.
- Integration tests with two-region staging that simulate partial packet loss and delayed kv diffs.
- Load tests to validate breaker thresholds and shedding order; evaluate false-positive breaker trips under high cold-cache scenarios.

Open trade-offs & risks:
- Consistency vs latency: full session state replication would prevent most resume pain but increases write latency and cost. We choose eventual-index + GSDH to balance cost and performance.
- SDK adoption: resumable streams require SDK changes; we will support HTTP/streaming fallback and provide server-side partial resume while SDKs roll out.
- Degraded-mode accuracy: serving quantized or stateless variants during fallback may change output. Need clear telemetry to detect quality regressions and fast rollback.

Current progress updates:
- 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with runtime, routing, SDK, and SRE. Agreed on GSDH handshake format and resume-token structure. (Aisha)
- 2026-03-04: Prototype resume-token server-side generation implemented; basic token replay logic unit-tested. (Calvin)
- 2026-03-08: Session-index schema v0 landed; replication uses low-rt replication pipeline. Increased storage cost estimate by ~6%. (Data infra)
- 2026-03-11: Circuit-breaker DSL v0 and simulation harness added; initial policy triggers validated in local chaos test. Observed one false-positive when cold-KV warming hit p99 spikes; tuning in progress. (SRE)

Next steps:
- Finish GSDH transfer of KV diffs and integrate into routing plane.
- Expand integration test matrix to include heterogeneous model families and long-lived streams.
- Prepare canary plan doc and communicate to customers with streaming SLAs before rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- In staging two-region test, session_resume_success >= 99.5% across 10k simulated stream failures.
- No increase >5% in average per-token latency for non-streaming p95 during normal operation.
- Runbook reviewed and practiced by SRE and on-call rotation.
